title: Mixing preserves Alice's input bits
statement: Let $\omega_X$ and $\omega_Y$ be two hard-distribution samples that share the same special coordinate $T$, whose Alice-inputs on the coordinates before $T$ agree, and whose Bob-inputs on the coordinates after $T$ agree. Then at every coordinate $i$, Alice's bit under the mixed sample $\mathrm{mix}(\omega_X,\omega_Y)$ equals Alice's bit under $\omega_X$ at that coordinate.
hypotheses_covered: the two samples have the same special coordinate T
the two samples' Alice-inputs before T agree (xBeforeSpecial equal)
the two samples' Bob-inputs after T agree (yAfterSpecial equal)
conclusion holds at every coordinate i
replaced: The mixed sample has Alice's input bits from the first sample.
